### Requirements

Claude Code is a command line tool that is platform independent.  Our consultants can install it on Windows, MacOS, or Linux at their discretion.  However, there are certain dependencies they will need prior to the training.

#### Development IDE

For this training, we will be using the Positron IDE, a VSCode clone specificly adapted to data science.  Positron is available for MacOS, Windows, and Linux and is a free download from Posit.  Participants can find it at the link below.  The remaining setup process will be through the TERMINAL section of Positron.  Many of our consultants are using SAS: the choice of this training in Positron/R is intentional because I want them to learn how to generate quality code without necessarily being proficient in that platform.  They will gain confidence in the AI and begin to develop an AI-specific set of validation skills.

https://positron.posit.co/download.html

#### Claude Code

Claude Code is a command line tool that is accessed through the TERMINAL section in Positron.  Participants can download it through a set of commands.

**Windows**

Open PowerShell in Positron's terminal and run the following commands. The first installs Node.js (which includes npm, required by Claude Code). Close and reopen the terminal after the Node.js install before running the second command.

```powershell
# Step 1 — Install Node.js LTS (includes npm)
winget install -e --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS

# Step 2 — Close and reopen the terminal, then install Claude Code
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

**MacOS/Linux**

Open the bash terminal in Positron and run the following commands.

*macOS:*

```bash
# Step 1 — Install Homebrew (skip if already installed)
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

# Step 2 — Install Node.js LTS (includes npm)
brew install node

# Step 3 — Install Claude Code
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

*Linux (Ubuntu/Debian):*

```bash
# Step 1 — Install Node.js LTS via NodeSource
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | sudo -E bash -
sudo apt-get install -y nodejs

# Step 2 — Install Claude Code
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

Once installed, users will need to login to their Anthropic account or access the models with an enterprise API key.  An Anthropic subscription is the most cost effective option and plans start at $25 a month and include hourly/daily/weekly limits.  API access is unlimited and billed by the token.  Provisioning this access should be completed prior to the first day of training.


#### Github

Consultants will need to access training materials through Github.  Github is a free online code repository that developers access to maintain their code.  It works like Track Changes for code development, every commit is tracked and users can look at their history to see every change and update they make over the lifecycle of a project and collaborate on projects.  I will develop a custom Github repository for the course and share it with the group.  The participants must create a Github account and configure it on their computers if they don't already have it.

1. Create a free account at [https://github.com](https://github.com) if you do not already have one.

2. Install Git on your computer.

   *Windows (PowerShell):*
   ```powershell
   winget install -e --id Git.Git
   ```

   *macOS (bash):*
   ```bash
   brew install git
   ```

   *Linux (bash):*
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install -y git
   ```

3. Configure Git with your name and the email address associated with your GitHub account. Run these in the Positron terminal:

   ```bash
   git config --global user.name "Your Name"
   git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
   ```

4. Generate an SSH key so your computer can authenticate to GitHub without a password. Run the command below, replacing the email with the one on your GitHub account. Press **Enter** to accept the default file location, then choose a passphrase (or press Enter twice to leave it blank).

   ```bash
   ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@example.com"
   ```

5. Copy your public key to the clipboard.

   *Windows (PowerShell):*
   ```powershell
   Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub" | Set-Clipboard
   ```

   *macOS (bash):*
   ```bash
   pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
   ```

   *Linux (bash):*
   ```bash
   cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
   # Manually select and copy the output
   ```

6. Add the key to GitHub:
   - Go to **github.com → Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key**
   - Give it a descriptive title (e.g., "Positron laptop")
   - Paste the key into the **Key** field and click **Add SSH key**

7. Test the connection:

   ```bash
   ssh -T git@github.com
   ```

   You should see: `Hi <username>! You've successfully authenticated...`

8. You will receive an invitation link to the course repository. Accept it, then clone the repository to your local machine using the SSH URL:

   ```bash
   git clone git@github.com:<repo-url-provided-by-instructor>.git
   ```

#### CDISC RAG Server

The course repository ships with a small search server that gives Claude direct access to CDISC controlled terminology — codelist definitions, valid values, and variable labels. Claude queries it whenever an exercise touches SDTM or ADaM variables, which is how it produces compliant code instead of guessing at terminology. It connects through MCP (Model Context Protocol), the standard Claude Code uses to talk to external tools.

The server needs its own dependencies installed. These are deliberately excluded from Git, so a fresh clone will **not** have them and the server will fail to start until you run the install below. Do this once, after cloning, from the terminal in Positron.

*Windows (PowerShell), macOS, and Linux (bash) — the same command works on all three:*

```bash
cd claude-training
npm install --prefix rag
```

You should see something like `added 93 packages`. Verify the server connects:

```bash
claude mcp list
```

Look for `cdisc-rag: node rag/server.js - ✔ Connected`.

**Troubleshooting.** If you see `✘ Failed to connect — CONNECTION_CLOSED`, the dependencies are missing or incomplete — re-run the `npm install --prefix rag` command above. To see the underlying error directly, run:

```bash
node rag/server.js
```

A message containing `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` confirms the dependencies are the problem. (This command starts the server and waits for input rather than returning to a prompt; press **Ctrl+C** to exit.)

Two other things to check if the install did not fix it:

- **Start Claude Code from the repository root.** The server is configured with a relative path, so launching `claude` from a different folder will not find it.
- **Reconnect an already-running session.** If Claude Code was open while you ran the install, it is still holding the failed connection. Type `/mcp` inside Claude Code to reconnect, or restart it.
